value.reason: The Evidence shows a direct path from the registration password to storage using a weak hash. In models/user.ts:70-75, the User model's password setter stores security.hash(clearTextPassword) through setDataValue('password', ...). In lib/insecurity.ts:41, hash is crypto.createHash('md5').update(data).digest('hex'). That is a single, unsalted MD5 digest, a fast hash with no key stretching and no salt. The data flow traces the password from the register form (register.component.html/ts), through user.service.ts POST to /api/Users, through the explicit server.ts middleware, and into the finale-generated model write that calls this setter. So user passwords are persisted as MD5 hashes. This matches the positive example (an md5 hash used for passwords) and differs from the negative example, where md5 is only used for an ETag. It is a clear instance of CWE-916. It also falls short of the reasonable security safeguards in DPDP Rule 6(1), because MD5 protection of authentication secrets is easy to crack offline after a breach.
